requestedIntent: Owner decision 2026-10-27: one model-choice rule for Claude and Codex agents in every host. A work-class table (critical, standard, mechanical, light, browser tour, trivial lookup) with the Claude model and the Codex model/effort for each, an effort section (four questions, levels, one-level escalation, no double payment), precedence of a project's recorded decision, waiting rules (background jobs, hand-off before long waits or past ~300k context, no watcher model), and an acef-note logging rule; the BMAD routing policy mapping follows the same table.
limitations: Wired, not enforced: nothing stops an ordinary Claude Code subagent or Codex run from using a higher class or effort than the table gives. Only actors admitted through ACEF routing (Full roles, Fix/Standard dispatches under admitted-role-routing-v1) are checked by the hard-wall hook, and they follow the routing policy, not the table.
Claude Code subagent effort comes from the agent definition frontmatter; ACEF ships no agent definitions per class, so the Claude effort levels apply only where a host defines them.
The Sol mapping (the latest Sol in the policy's families map) is carried over from the V327-CAL-001 calibration of an earlier Sol without recalibration.

Admitted roles on anthropic follow per-role models: development, ATDD, the Conductor and Code Review resolve to Sonnet through their class; Patch Assurance and both Judges resolve to Opus through roleModels (owner decision 2026-10-27; cost note: review roles only). A host changes a role in its policy copy or per run with acef-state active-run --routing-role-model; review roles never go below the ACEF-owned floors (method/model-review-floors-v1.json) without a recorded owner exemption.
Effect not measured: no host has recorded model and effort per report yet, so the weekly retro has no effort comparison.

The newer-model check reads only the local Codex model cache, so it covers Codex families (Sol, Astra, Terra); Claude ids are updated by hand in the policy. acef-version-check reports a newer version; Ram decides the map change.
acef-model-id-scan runs on ACEF through selfcheck and test-acef-model-routing; host coordinators run it themselves (--root <host>) until their scripts move to the resolver.

evidence.note: 2026-10-27: openai roles resolve to gpt-6.1-sol; every anthropic class maps to claude-sonnet-5-5 (per-role Opus defaults: see the roleModels entry below); policy note names MODEL_CHOICE.md.

2026-10-27 roleModels: anthropic development, atdd, conductor and code-review resolve to claude-sonnet-5-5 (class); patch-assurance, process-judge and epic-process-judge resolve to claude-opus-5-5 (roleModels); openai stays gpt-6.1-sol for every role.

2026-11-28 model families: providers.<id>.families is the one place exact ids live; openai class models equal families.sol; acef-model resolves families and roles (empty stdout on failure, family fall-through past a whole-file override); acef-version-check reports newer cache versions from a fixture cache without changing its exit code; acef-model-id-scan finds literal ids outside the policy and ACEF has none.
2026-11-28: install-acef-tools installs .acef/bin/acef-model; the installed copy prints families.sol and the review role's model and effort from the installed policy.
